statement: A health survey asked $40$ adults how many minutes they exercised yesterday. The results are summarized in the table. $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Minutes} & \text{Number of adults} \\ \hline 0 \text{ to less than } 10 & 5 \\ 10 \text{ to less than } 20 & 8 \\ 20 \text{ to less than } 30 & 6 \\ 30 \text{ to less than } 40 & 9 \\ 40 \text{ to less than } 50 & 12 \end{array}$$ Which interval contains the median number of minutes?

choices.misconception: I found the median of the counts 5, 8, 6, 9 and 12, which is 8, and picked the row with 8 adults instead of finding the middle adult.
I picked the middle row of the table, but the median is the middle adult, and the rows do not hold equal numbers of adults.
I picked the row with the most adults, 12, but that is the modal interval, not the one holding the median.

hints: The median of $40$ values is halfway between the $20$th and $21$st values in order.
Keep a running total down the table until you pass $20$ adults.
The running totals are $5$, $13$, $19$, $28$, $40$. The $20$th and $21$st adults come after the first $19$.

solutions.reliable: The median of $40$ values is the average of the $20$th and $21$st values. The running totals are $5, 13, 19, 28, 40$. The first $19$ adults are in the first three intervals, and adults $20$ through $28$ are in the interval $30$ to less than $40$. Both middle values are there, so the median is in $30$ to less than $40$ minutes.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
